elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor or otherwise burdening Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 7.2 expressly states that “Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.”

elements.element: Any most-favoured-nation obligation burdening Customer is limited to an expressly defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: revised Section 7.2 eliminates any MFN obligation benefiting Vendor, so no broader product scope applies.

elements.element: Any most-favoured-nation obligation burdening Customer lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: because revised Section 7.2 imposes no MFN obligation, there is no MFN duration exceeding 12 months.

elements.element: Any most-favoured-nation obligation burdening Customer contains carve-outs excluding transactions or terms that are not reasonably comparable.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: revised Section 7.2 imposes no MFN comparison obligation at all, so Customer cannot be required to match non-comparable transactions or terms.

result.reason: The operative revision completely removes the MFN obligation burdening Customer and is consistent with the unchanged acknowledgment in Section 12.3. The fallback limitations are independently satisfied because the underlying MFN obligation is expressly absent. Only Section 7.2 was changed, no unrelated obligation was added, and the remaining commercial terms continue to operate without contradiction.
